clue.text: Confused indeed if unit is not named

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled, so the three words indeed, if, unit are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a unit whose name is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges INDEED, IF and UNIT, twelve letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not named has no identity attached; it is anonymous.

clue.text: Faint when a relative arrives?

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
ar, short for arrives, appears on timetables

explanation.surface: Feeling faint when a family member turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something faint is indistinct or not plain to see.

clue.text: It's awkward to kip in it

indicators.note: in puts the sleep word inside the word it

parts.note: kip is British slang for a nap

explanation.surface: Sleeping on the job is awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or clumsy, out of place.

clue.text: Showing affection in a roundabout sort of way

definitions.text: Showing affection in a roundabout sort of way

parts.words: Showing affection in a roundabout sort of way
parts.note: roundabout suggests indirectness, but here means literally encircling someone with the arms

explanation.definitionFit: A hug wraps the arms around another person as a sign of love.

clue.text: Attempt to grab a carrier

indicators.note: to grab means the attempt word closes around the letter

parts.note: an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Trying to seize a carrier bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray is a flat board for carrying food or drinks.

clue.text: Clerk content among office-workers — all time-wasters

clue.text: A little yet weighty figure

indicators.note: a little of the word weighty means only some of its letters are taken

explanation.surface: A small number that is nonetheless heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a number, and figure is another word for a numeral.

clue.text: One due for release after a stretch is shy

definitions.text: One due for release after a stretch

explanation.surface: A prisoner awaiting release after a jail term, timid about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch' suggests a prison sentence, but a catapult's elastic is stretched before release; shy means to hurl.
explanation.definitionFit: A slingshot is drawn back then let go, and to shy is to throw or fling.

clue.text: Guard appearing fed-up over tip

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word fed is read from bottom to top

parts.note: fed is taken as written
a tip is an end

explanation.surface: A sentry who is fed up with his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses FED to DEF in a down clue; 'over' places it above END.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend is to protect or keep safe.

clue.text: Applaud the directors facing the house?

parts.note: to applaud is to clap
a company's directors together form its board

explanation.surface: Cheering the board of directors as they face the shareholders.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: clapboard is wooden weatherboarding that faces (covers) the outside of a house; 'house' tempts a theatre reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapboard is overlapping timber cladding used on the outer walls of buildings.

clue.text: Bars put right in the entrance

indicators.note: in places the letter for right inside the word for the entrance

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Bars correctly fitted in a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire grate is made of metal bars.

clue.text: Take two-thirds of the men by some other way

indicators.note: keeping two of the three letters of the word for the men drops one of them

parts.note: the men simply gives the word men

indicators.note: read the other way, the word for some runs backwards

parts.note: some, as in a portion, is part

explanation.surface: An instruction to take two-thirds of the men by a different route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds of' trims MEN to EN; 'other way' turns PART (some) into TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To take an animal or person by stealth is to catch them, a sense of snare.

clue.text: Sporting event of no interest to certain folk

parts.note: something flat is dull and of no interest
a race is a particular group of people

explanation.surface: A sports fixture that bores some people.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat race is a horse race run without jumps, a fixture of the turf.

clue.text: Social reformer making a variety of baby-food popular

parts.note: a rusk is a hard biscuit given to teething babies
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A campaigner who popularises a kind of baby food.
explanation.walkthrough: John Ruskin was a Victorian art critic and social thinker; a rusk is a dry biscuit for babies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian writer argued for social and economic reform in works such as Unto This Last.

clue.text: Picture biscuits that are crisp and spicy

parts.note: ginger snaps are crisp biscuits
spicy food is hot

explanation.surface: A tempting image of crunchy ginger biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick informal photograph.

clue.text: This is intellectually deep for cast

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so for
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: Something deep enough for a cast of actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound ideas show great insight and depth of thought.

clue.text: Replacing cracked tea-set as a preliminary

parts.note: for can mean in place of, as in a substitute for

indicators.note: cracked suggests the tea-set broken and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Buying a new tea service after the old one broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample of what is to come.

clue.text: Write letters in bed in quarters

parts.note: in is taken as written

indicators.note: the second in places the bed inside the two compass points

parts.note: S and E, south and east, are compass quarters
a crib is a child's bed

explanation.surface: Writing letters from one's bed in lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' are compass points, S and E, with CRIB put inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe is to engrave or write words on a surface.

clue.text: Giving a signal when slowing down

explanation.surface: Waving a flag while losing pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagging is signalling with a flag, and also tiring or weakening.

clue.text: Burning to include bill for carriage

indicators.note: to include means the burning word surrounds the bill

parts.note: burning is fire
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: An arsonist charged for a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A fiacre is a small hired horse-drawn carriage, named after a Paris hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: This French hackney coach was a horse-drawn vehicle for hire.

clue.text: Spoke of alternative date possibly

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: possibly suggests the word date in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: Talking about a different date.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak formally in public, giving a speech, is to orate.

clue.text: The fall of the French currency

parts.note: des is French for of the, plural
a cent is a unit of currency

explanation.surface: The collapse of the French currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a downward movement or drop.

clue.text: Bishop interrupts because religious treatise is unrealistic

indicators.note: the bishop's letter breaks into the word for because

parts.note: as can mean because
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a tract is a short religious pamphlet

explanation.surface: A bishop interrupts because a religious pamphlet is impractical.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract thought deals in ideas rather than concrete reality.

clue.text: Hood's puttin' on vestments

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's band dressing up.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood is the English outlaw; puttin' drops its g, so robin' is robing with the g lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw's first name, and robing (putting on robes) with its final letter dropped.

clue.text: Doesn't allow much shade in an ocean-going vessel

indicators.note: in puts the shade inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a tint is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Someone stingy with paint colour aboard a liner.
explanation.definitionFit: To stint is to be sparing, giving only a little.

clue.text: A woman's aim on changing

indicators.note: changing indicates the letters of aim on being rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman's goal shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female first name, from the Book of Ruth.

clue.text: Opening-with a key, it follows

indicators.note: follows means it comes after the preceding letters

parts.note: D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A door opening with a key behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is an entrance passage into a mine.

clue.text: Greek character goes to the doctor for a lozenge

parts.note: rho is the Greek letter R
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A Greek visiting the doctor for a throat sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb is a rhombus, the diamond shape also called a lozenge.

clue.text: One's dip is put off — cause to feel badly

indicators.note: put off suggests the letters are disturbed and placed differently

parts.note: the possessive s is counted here as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged from a swim, made to feel unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' rearranges ONES, DIP and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To indispose is to make slightly ill or disinclined.

clue.text: He can make people lose all sense

definitions.text: He can make people lose all sense

parts.words: He can make people lose all sense
parts.note: reads like an annoying talker, but means a doctor who removes all sensation, the original sense of feeling

explanation.definitionFit: This medical specialist puts patients under so they feel nothing during surgery.
